question.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{″}-y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $2$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

*Hint: You may assume that all the sine coefficients in the Fourier series of the particular solution are equal to zero.*

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{{field-1}}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)
$$
question.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}n\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi x))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{″}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation and have

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)-(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x))=1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
-\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}(-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}-1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x)=1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x).
$$

Now, equating the free terms and cosine coefficients, we obtain:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=1 \\ {a}_{n}(-{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}-1)=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{3}\pi }\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=-1 \\ {a}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼-1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{(-1)^{n}}{{n}^{3}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+1)}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi x).
$$
